content.comment_body: The [product_name] basis module ([article_no]), after years of operation, entered STOP mode. I have tried turning the power off and on again, but only the additional module returns to RUN mode. If this module needs to be replaced, which model should I use, since it's no longer available since 2018? Hope someone can assist.

The current replacement model is [article_no]. To use it, you need the latest [product_name] software ([version_no]). You can update this for free if you have an older version. However, you cannot use the expansion modules from [article_no] with the new [product_name], so you would need to purchase new ones.

The modules are not programmed—they just switch lights on and off with push buttons. Is there any way to repair or reset the modules? The setup includes one power module with an RCo and extension for all ground-floor lights and screens, and another RCo with extension for the upstairs lights. The upstairs module remains red, while its extension is green but not functioning, resulting in no lights upstairs.

Diagnosing a [product_name] module without a display is challenging. The only method is to use [product_name] software and a programming cable for this module, which lets you check its status or upload a backup. If you need the exact same module, try searching online marketplaces or contact [company_name] for a spare part, although it will likely cost more than newer versions.
If the [product_name] remains in STOP mode, simply switching the power off and on is not sufficient. Connect it with the [product_name] software and attempt to start the program from there.
Issue resolved. Setting the module to RUN using the program alone did not work. I created and uploaded a new program, and now the module is operational. Thanks for the support.

analysis.insight_summary: A user faced an issue where a [product_name] module unexpectedly switched to STOP mode after years of service, causing a loss of lighting control. Power cycling did not restore functionality, and troubleshooting was complicated by the lack of display and diagnostic options. Community members recommended using management software and replacing hardware due to end-of-life status, illustrating ongoing challenges with maintenance and component compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for straightforward repair or reset solutions for the [product_name] module after a STOP fault, aiming for quick functionality restoration without needing complex diagnostics or major replacements.
